title: Neural Network Interpretability: LIME and SHAP
description: Why interpretability matters for transparent AI, and how LIME and SHAP explain predictions - with local surrogate models versus fair, game-theory-based feature attributions.
content:
**Neural network interpretability** is crucial for understanding how models make predictions and ensuring transparency in AI systems.

Two widely used interpretability techniques are:
• LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations)
• SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations)

**LIME** provides local interpretability, meaning it explains individual predictions by approximating the model with a simpler surrogate model. LIME perturbs the input data slightly and observes how the model's prediction changes, then fits a simple linear model to these perturbed examples, approximating the original model's behavior in a local region. Features with the highest coefficients in the linear model are considered the most important for that specific instance.

**SHAP** is based on Shapley values, a concept from cooperative game theory, to distribute the importance of features fairly across all predictions. SHAP assigns a value to each feature, representing its contribution to a model's prediction. It considers different combinations of features to evaluate their impact, and the Shapley value is computed by averaging over the possible feature contributions. SHAP provides both local and global interpretability.

In short: LIME explains one prediction at a time by locally imitating the model with a simple linear surrogate, while SHAP fairly splits the prediction's credit among features using game theory - and extends to global explanations as well.
